description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue for U.S. pharmaceutical plants (HVAC, fume hoods, cleanrooms, motors, compressed air, pumps, refrigeration, lighting, steam, CHP); almost every number is reprinted from other sources and there are no energy intensities per unit of product. Not loaded: Figures 5-7 (charts, values not printed), company and state tables (Tables 1-2), qualitative measures, Appendices A-C.

author: Brinkmann, T., Giner Santonja, G., Yukseler, H., Roudier, S. and Delgado Sancho, L.
title: Best Available Techniques (BAT) Reference Document for Common Waste Water and Waste Gas Treatment/Management Systems in the Chemical Sector
description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Targeted pass of a 664-page BREF. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 30). Data are mostly EU (DE, FR, NL plant examples); some cost figures reprinted from US EPA (2003, 2008) fact sheets and older national sources (NOREC 2000, VITO 2010, InfoMil 1999, ETBPP 1996, Biothane 2000). Loaded: effluent treatment - complete-mix activated sludge, SBR, MBR and fixed-bed biofilter costs (Table 3.121); activated sludge WWTP energy per m3 and per kg COD abated and survey cost ranges (Tables 3.130, 3.133); MBR example plants Aramon (Table 3.137, costs p.315) and Roche Penzberg (p.315); UASB anaerobic pretreatment cost (Table 3.111, capacity derived from printed volume, load and COD); air and steam stripping (Tables 3.98, 3.101); evaporation steam ratio (Table 3.93); wet air oxidation costs (Table 3.63). Waste gas - straight, regenerative and recuperative thermal oxidisers (energy Table 3.202, costs Table 3.206 with column attribution checked against the US EPA footnote numbers), catalytic oxidisers (Tables 3.208, 3.211), elevated flares (Table 3.298) and four German central waste-gas incineration plants (Table 3.299: capex, stack flow; hourly consumables and stack CO2 in other-values). Not loaded: pollutant concentrations, abatement efficiencies and BAT-AELs (non-GHG), particulate and inorganic-gas abatement, monitoring, diffuse VOC, odour, noise, sludge thickening, Chapter 5 emerging techniques (pollutant-specific, bench or single-site; no energy-relevant data), Figure 2.7 (chart only). description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Targeted pass of a 392-page BREF (printed page = PDF page - 28 throughout). Locators are PRINTED page numbers. author: Danish Energy Agency and Energinet
title: Technology Data - Generation of Electricity and District Heating (version 0019)
description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Produced by _high/_work/scratch-dea_2026_technology-data-electricity-district-heat/extract.py from the individual datasheets of the workbook (not alldata_long: its 40 Comp. hp, airsource 10 MW COP and nameplate rows (2.7/2.5) differ from the datasheet (2.8/2.6); all other 17,000 values agree). Scope: industry-relevant heat and CHP technologies only - 59 datasheets: 01 coal extraction CHP, 04/05 gas turbines (simple cycle with heat recovery, combined cycle), 06 gas engines, 08 waste-to-energy CHP and HOP, 09 biomass CHP (back-pressure and extraction) and HOP, 10 Stirling gasified biomass, 11 SOFC and 12 PEM fuel-cell CHP, 20 onshore wind (utility; for the wind-turbine gap), 22 commercial/industrial rooftop PV+BESS (for the photovoltaic-array_battery-storage gap), 40 compression heat pumps, 41 electric boilers, 44 gas and 47 oil DH boilers, 45 geothermal DH with heat pump, 46 solar DH, 50-52 peak plants. Skipped: 02 life-time extension and 03 coal-to-biomass conversions (power-plant retrofits), 21 offshore wind, other 22 PV sheets, 20 domestic turbines, 23 wave. Base year: 2025 where the sheet prints a 2025 central value (20, 22, 40, 41, 45, 47), else 2020 (all other sheets; no 2025 column). Lower/upper loaded as value-min/max only when printed for the same year: 2020 sheets have 2020 ranges; the 2025 sheets 40/41/45/47 print ranges only for 2030 and 2050, so they have no range; 20 onshore prints ranges for 2020 only. Ranges equal to the central value are dropped. All other years go to _projections.csv (the DEA convention in this folder). Loaded: capacity (MW_e electric-output for CHP and power; MW_h thermal-output for heat-only), net annual-average electrical and heat efficiency (target electricity/heat for CHP; blank target for heat-only, = COP for heat pumps), name-plate efficiency only where no annual average is printed (01 coal, 10 Stirling), lifetime, construction time, minimum load, availability/capacity factor/degradation where printed, CH4 and N2O per GJ fuel input (CO2 is not printed), capex = Nominal investment (*total) per MW (M EUR/MW x1000 to EUR/kW), fixed O&M (EUR/MW/y /1000 to EUR/kW-yr), variable O&M per MWh output (for heat-only sheets with a split, the 'other O&M' row, i.e. excluding the auxiliary electricity cost). Derived: heat-to-power-ratio = 1/Cb (Cb printed; back-pressure mode); efficiency-chp = electrical + heat annual average for back-pressure CHP (report note H: total efficiency is their sum); PV capacity factor = AC full-load hours/8760; temperature-output from the DH forward temperature in the sheet title (40, 45 and large 08/09 sheets). Flows: auxiliary electricity per GJ heat for heat-only boilers and solar DH (not included in their efficiency, guideline p.23); for heat pumps and geothermal it is inside the COP (notes D/M) and goes to _other-values. _other-values: name-plate efficiencies, equipment/installation splits, per-MW-input and per-tonne-input costs of biomass/WtE CHP (note J: not additive to the per-MW_e cost), outages, Cb/Cv, condensate, fuel-storage cost, start-up costs, geothermal well and heat-pump split, PV/battery details. Not extracted: SO2/NOx/particles (non-GHG), regulation and start-up times, space requirement, binary design flags, per-DC PV rows. Locators: 'report p.N' is the PDF page, which equals the table-of-contents page numbers (pages carry no printed number); the 11 SOFC and 12 PEMFC chapters are not in the v0019 report (datasheets only). All efficiencies of thermal plants are on LHV (guideline p.22); emissions per GJ fuel at LHV (p.25). COST BASIS overnight = EPC/overnight price incl. on-site infrastructure, excluding owners' costs and interest during construction (guideline p.25-26); onshore wind is total-plant (includes land, neighbour settlements, decommissioning of old turbines and construction loan interest, note H).

Loaded (main file): engine/motor/fuel-cell/H2-ICE efficiencies (Sect. 2), tractor and excavator system efficiencies (final to useful energy), diesel construction capex 1400 EUR2025/kW, agricultural diesel capex DKK/kW by machine type and size class (Table 9, one row per size class with a leading [size] case marker), BEV abatement cost (EUR2025/t CO2), TRLs per construction size segment and for hydrogen machines, state-of-development for HVO, ag BEV, methane and hydrogen, methane CO2/N2O reduction vs diesel. author: Joshi, J.U. and Bolech, M.
institution: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency and TNO
title: Decarbonisation options for the Dutch onshore gas and oil industry (MIDDEN)
description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Page numbers are the printed page numbers, which equal PDF page numbers. The report gives few per-unit technology parameters: it is mostly a sector emissions inventory plus option descriptions. Loaded: gas-turbine compressor efficiency assumption (33%) and per-kWh-output CO2/CH4; electric compressor drive efficiency (99% x 95%), unit sizes (Groningen GLT 23 MW, Wijngaarden 10 MW) and costs (GLT first cluster US$70m2018; EPA 2011 four 1.3 MW US$9.4m2018, O&M 10%); mobile recompression unit (225 kW, ~1% fuel per gas recovered, EUR2018 2m first-unit capex, O&M 10%); gas receiving station preheating: conventional water-bath outlet temperature, vortex tube + ground heat exchanger (80-88% gas saving), flat-plate solar (8-12%, US$2018 153k), evacuated-tube solar + MTG-550 turboexpander (Tables 7-8); cryogenic ASU electricity for nitrogen (0.16-0.30 and 0.35-0.55 kWh/m3). Mobile flaring, LDAR and zero-emission valves get description rows only (paybacks in _measures). Not loaded (in _other-values): facility/sector emissions and NG use (Tables 1, 2, 4), grid-dependent electric-compressor savings, Schoonebeek CHP plant data (no output), blue-hydrogen footprint assumptions, hydrogen network costs. Not extracted: Figures 1-21 (charts), Appendix 1 equations, Table 3/5/10 (qualitative or sector totals). No dehydration, gas treating, CCS or line-heater-at-wellsite numbers: the report refers to Tamez & Dellaert (2020) for those. Most cost and performance numbers are reprinted from foreign case studies (EPA 2011 USA, Ghezelbash 2016 Iran, Farzaneh-Gord Iran, Barone 2019 Italy).
